processing: Ripe pu-erh: sun-dried Yunnan large-leaf material goes through wet piling, as with all shu, and is then pressed. The exact blend behind the number is not published in detail.
harvest_season: Not stated for this recipe. Ripe pu-erh blends typically draw on material from several pickings.
appearance_dry: Dark brown pressed leaf with a mix of buds and more mature leaves, going by a tasting of the 2023 edition.
appearance_liquor: Deep, bright red in the early steeps, thinning to lighter amber after about the seventh, going by one tasting of the 2023 edition.
appearance_wet: Soft, dark brown leaf and buds, as is typical of ripe pu-erh.
taste_profile: Sweet, smooth and full in the middle steeps, slightly heavy at first and flatter toward the end, with woody and caramel notes on the dry leaf.

brewing.notes: Typical ripe pu-erh method: rinse once, use water just off the boil, and keep the first steeps short because the liquor thickens quickly.

vintage_note: Sold by production year under the same number: a 2008 lot in 100 g and a 2023 commemorative edition in 357 g are both on record. Like other ripe pu-erh it is drunk young or kept for some years, and older dry-stored lots are resold by collectors. Always check the year, since one number covers quite different pressings.
description:
0085 is a numbered ripe pu-erh from Lancang Gucha, a Yunnan factory with its roots in Lancang county. The number works like a recipe name, though what it stands for is not publicly explained.

Little is documented about the blend itself. One detailed tasting of the 2023 commemorative edition describes material from the Jingmai area, with buds and leaves together and some maturity to them. Whether that holds for other years is not known, so treat each year as its own tea.

That same tasting found woody, caramel-sweet dry leaf, then a deep red cup, slightly heavy at first, most balanced in the middle steeps and flatter toward the end. The taster preferred the livelier 2022 edition. Brew it as you would any ripe pu-erh: hot water and short steeps at the start.

When buying, look at the wrapper year and the weight, and be wary of resale claims. Secondhand listings lean on phrases like market-recognised quality and dry storage, which you cannot check from a photo. A sample before a whole cake is the sensible way in.
history:
Lancang Gucha traces its brand to 1966. By the company's account, its predecessor factory went bankrupt in 1998, and Du Chunyi and 82 laid-off workers raised 390,000 yuan to form the present company.

Little is documented about 0085 specifically. A 2008 lot appears in resale listings and a 2023 commemorative edition in tasting notes, but when the recipe began and how it changed are not on public record.
